# 5-Agent Customer Support Weekly Coverage Plan

## Shift Rotation and Coverage Grid
This sample assumes a simple 8-hour shift model with a 1-hour lunch inside the shift, and staggered start times to keep coverage steady from **8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday–Friday**.

| Agent | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Weekly Hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent A | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 40 |
| Agent B | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 40 |
| Agent C | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 40 |
| Agent D | 10:00–18:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 40 |
| Agent E | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 10:00–18:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 8:00–16:00 | 40 |

## Coverage Logic and Risk Check
**Coverage model**
- Each shift is **8 hours total**, including a **1-hour lunch** and two short breaks.
- Use a lunch rotation so only **one agent is on lunch at a time**.
- Stagger lunches into three windows: **11:30–12:30, 12:00–1:00, 12:30–1:30**.
- With 5 agents on staff and 2 people on the later shift most days, you can keep **at least 2 agents available at all times**, including during one lunch break.

**Break coverage logic**
- Early shift agents cover the morning demand from **8:00–10:00**.
- Mid/late shift overlap begins at **10:00**, which protects the busiest midday period.
- Schedule lunches so the team always has:
  - **3 agents available** when one is on lunch and one is handling a spike
  - **2 agents minimum** during lower-volume periods
- Assign one agent daily as the **lunch coordinator** to confirm breaks do not overlap.

**Staffing gaps or risks**
- **Tight at peak volume:** If call/chat volume spikes at lunch or near close, the schedule has little buffer beyond the minimum 2-agent requirement.
- **No true backup:** With all 5 agents scheduled at 40 hours, there is no spare capacity for sick leave, training, or meetings.
- **Close-of-day risk:** The **5:00–6:00 PM** window can become fragile if one late shift agent is pulled into a long case.
- **Adherence sensitivity:** If one agent returns late from lunch, the “one lunch at a time” rule can slip quickly.

**Best-practice adjustment**
- Keep one agent per day designated as a **floater/backup owner** for escalations.
- If possible, add a part-time backup or flex hour block for absences and overflow.
